examples.en: A small pond sits in the middle of the park.
An old church stood on top of the hill.

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 큰 나무가 자리한 모습이 예뻐요.
examples.en: The sight of the big tree at the village entrance is pretty.
That cafe is at the end of the alley.

examples.ko: 강 옆에 자리한 집에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to live in a house by the river.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 시장 안쪽에 자리하고 있어서 찾기 어려워요.
examples.en: That restaurant is deep inside the market, so it is hard to find.

explain: '위치하다'와 거의 같고, '있다'보다 글이나 안내문 같은 느낌이에요. 여행 소개, 뉴스에서 '~에 자리한 ~'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 나와요. 주어는 보통 건물, 가게, 장소예요.

phrases.example: 그때 들은 말이 아직도 제 마음속에 자리하고 있어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소가 아니라 기억이나 감정이 마음에 남아 있다는 뜻으로 써요. 글이나 노래 가사에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not for a place but for a memory or feeling that stays inside you. Common in writing and song lyrics.
phrases.en_equiv: to live on in one's heart

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '위치하다' and sounds more like writing or signage than plain '있다'. It often appears in travel guides and news in the modifying form '~에 자리한 ~' (the ~ located at ~). The subject is usually a building, shop or place.

examples.ko: 방 안에 책상을 창문 쪽으로 배치해요.
examples.en: I arrange the desk toward the window in the room.

examples.ko: 가게 입구에 의자를 두 개 배치했어요.
examples.en: We placed two chairs at the entrance of the shop.

examples.ko: 가구를 다르게 배치하면 방이 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: If you arrange the furniture differently, the room looks bigger.
They placed guides all around the airport.
The coach is thinking about where to place the players.

examples.ko: 신입 사원을 다음 달에 영업팀에 배치할 거예요.
examples.en: We will assign the new employee to the sales team next month.

explain: '놓다'나 '두다'는 그냥 놓는 일이고, '배치하다'는 어디에 둘지 생각해서 자리를 정하는 느낌이에요. 물건뿐 아니라 사람에게도 써서 '직원을 배치하다'라고 해요. 명사 '배치'는 '자리 배치', '좌석 배치'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '놓다' and '두다' just mean putting something down, while 'baechihada' implies deciding where each thing goes. It works for people too, as in '직원을 배치하다' (assign staff). The noun '배치' appears in '자리 배치' (seating plan) and '좌석 배치' (seat layout).

examples.en: I saw the Seoul night view from Namsan Tower.
You go up to the top of the tower by elevator.
That tall tower is a famous tourist spot.
I took photos with my friends in front of the tower.
A new tower has been built in this city.
Inside the tower there is an observatory and a restaurant.

explain: 옛 절에 있는 돌탑이나 전통 건축물은 '탑', 현대의 높은 전망 건물은 '타워'라고 불러요. '남산타워', '롯데월드타워'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙는 일이 많아요. 방송이나 통신용 높은 건물에도 '타워'를 써요.
explain_en: Stone pagodas at old temples and traditional structures are '탑', while tall modern observation buildings are 'tower'. It usually attaches to a name, as in '남산타워' or '롯데월드타워'. It is also used for tall broadcast and communication structures.

examples.en: I go to the baseball stadium with a friend on weekends.
I watched the game while eating chicken at the baseball stadium.
It is very crowded in front of the baseball stadium.

examples.ko: 우리 집에서 야구장까지 지하철로 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes thirty minutes from my home to the baseball stadium by subway.
The newly built baseball stadium is really big.
At the baseball stadium I sang along loudly to the cheering songs.

explain: '종목 이름 + 장'으로 만들어서 야구장, 축구장, 농구장, 골프장이라고 해요. 야구장은 응원가를 함께 부르고 치킨 같은 간식을 먹으며 보는 분위기로 유명해요. 경기를 하는 곳을 두루 부르는 말은 '경기장'이에요.
explain_en: Korean forms these by adding '장' to the sport: 야구장, 축구장, 농구장, 골프장. Baseball parks are known for fans singing cheering songs together and snacking on things like fried chicken. The general word for any sports venue is '경기장'.

examples.en: I climbed up to the roof on a ladder.
I need a ladder to change the light bulb.
Please lean the ladder against the wall.

examples.ko: 이 사다리는 이 층까지 닿기에는 너무 짧아요.
examples.en: This ladder is too short to reach the second floor.

examples.ko: 제가 올라가는 동안 아버지가 사다리를 잡아 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father held the ladder while I climbed up.
The firefighter rescued people with a ladder.

explain: 계단은 건물에 붙어 있고, 사다리는 옮겨서 쓰는 도구예요. 올라갈 때는 '오르다'도 쓰지만 '사다리를 타다'가 더 자연스러워요. 세우거나 걸칠 때는 '사다리를 세우다', '사다리를 걸치다'를 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 세로줄을 고르고 가로줄을 따라 내려가 결과를 정하는 제비뽑기 놀이예요. 누가 살지, 누가 청소할지 정할 때 친구들끼리 많이 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drawing-lots game where you pick a vertical line and follow the rungs down to see the result. Friends use it to decide who pays or who cleans.

explain_en: Stairs are fixed to a building, while a ladder is a portable tool. You can say '오르다' (climb) but '사다리를 타다' sounds more natural. To set one up you say '사다리를 세우다' (stand up) or '사다리를 걸치다' (rest against).

examples.ko: 여행 가이드가 유명한 맛집을 소개해 줬어요.
examples.en: The tour guide recommended a famous restaurant to us.
I toured Gyeongbokgung, following the guide.
The guide was very kind, so it was nice.
I would like to book a guide who speaks English.

examples.ko: 가이드가 길을 알려 줘서 길을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: The guide showed us the way, so we did not get lost.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 가이드 없이 혼자 제주도를 여행해요.
examples.en: Next week I will travel around Jeju alone without a guide.

explain: 여행을 안내하는 사람을 '가이드'라고 하고, '투어 가이드'라고도 해요. 책은 '가이드북', 지켜야 할 기준은 '가이드라인'이라서 비슷하게 들려도 쓰임이 달라요. 박물관에서 설명해 주는 사람은 '도슨트'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: A person who leads tours is a 'guide', also 'tour guide' (투어 가이드). A book is a '가이드북' and a set of standards is a '가이드라인', so they sound alike but are used differently. Someone who explains exhibits in a museum is often called a '도슨트'.

examples.en: A helicopter is flying in the sky.
Yesterday I rode in a helicopter for the first time.
A helicopter landed on the mountain.
The sound of the helicopter is too loud.
The child likes the toy helicopter.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 헬리콥터로 환자를 옮기는 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a scene on the news of a patient being moved by helicopter.

explain: 말할 때는 '헬기'로 줄여서 자주 말해요. 산불 진화나 구조 뉴스에서 많이 들리는 말이에요. 탈 때는 '타다', 하늘로 오를 때는 '뜨다', 땅에 내릴 때는 '착륙하다'를 같이 써요.
explain_en: In speech Koreans often shorten it to '헬기'. You hear it a lot in news about wildfires and rescues. The usual verbs are '타다' (ride), '뜨다' (take off) and '착륙하다' (land).

examples.en: Please write your name on the back of the paper.
The phone number is on the back of the card.
I tossed a coin in the game and it came up tails.
I wrote the date on the back of the photo.

examples.ko: 숟가락 뒷면으로 달걀 껍데기를 살짝 두드려요.
examples.en: I lightly tap the eggshell with the back of a spoon.

examples.ko: 지갑 뒷면에 작은 주머니가 하나 더 있어요.
examples.en: There is one more small pocket on the back of the wallet.

explain: 납작한 물건에는 '앞면/뒷면', 방향에는 '앞쪽/뒤쪽'을 써요. 'ㅅ' 받침을 넣어 '뒷면'이라고 쓰고 [뒨면]으로 소리 나요. 동전 던지기를 할 때도 '앞면이 나왔어요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Use '앞면/뒷면' for flat objects and '앞쪽/뒤쪽' for directions. It is spelled with the extra 'ㅅ' (뒷면) and pronounced [dwin-myeon]. In a coin toss, people say '앞면이 나왔어요' (it came up heads).

examples.en: This cafe has a really pretty interior.

examples.ko: 새집 인테리어를 어떻게 할지 고민하고 있어요.
examples.en: I am thinking about how to do the interior of my new home.

examples.ko: 우리 가게 인테리어 공사가 한 달이나 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The interior renovation of our shop took a whole month.

examples.ko: 저는 인테리어 사진을 보는 걸 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like looking at interior design photos.
I decided to go in after seeing the restaurant's interior.

examples.ko: 인테리어를 바꾸고 나서 집이 훨씬 밝아졌어요.
examples.en: After changing the interior, the house became much brighter.

explain: 집이나 가게를 새로 고칠 때 '인테리어를 하다'라고 자주 말해요. 공사까지 크게 하면 '인테리어 공사', 분위기를 칭찬할 때는 '인테리어가 예쁘다'라고 해요. '실내장식'이라는 말도 있지만 훨씬 딱딱해서 일상에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: When fixing up a home or shop, Koreans often say '인테리어를 하다'. A big job is '인테리어 공사' (renovation work), and for praise you say '인테리어가 예쁘다'. The word '실내장식' exists but is much stiffer and rare in daily talk.

examples.ko: 목포는 한반도의 남서쪽 끝에 있는 바닷가 도시예요.
examples.en: Mokpo is a seaside city at the southwestern end of the Korean Peninsula.
Today the wind blows from the southwest.
The southwest sky has turned red.

examples.ko: 학교에서 남서쪽으로 오 분만 걸으면 저희 집이에요.
examples.en: If you walk five minutes southwest from the school, you reach my house.
Look for the southwest direction on the map.

examples.ko: 이 산의 남서쪽 길은 경사가 심해요.
examples.en: The southwest trail of this mountain is steep.

explain: 방위 이름은 '북동, 북서, 남동, 남서'처럼 북·남을 먼저 말해요. '남서쪽에서 불다'는 출발점, '남서쪽으로 가다'는 가는 방향이라 조사가 달라요. 같은 방향을 '서남쪽'이라고 하는 사람도 있어요.
explain_en: Korean compass names put north or south first: 북동, 북서, 남동, 남서. The particles differ: '남서쪽에서 불다' (blow from) marks the starting point, '남서쪽으로 가다' (go toward) the direction. Some people also say '서남쪽' for the same direction.

examples.en: That village is in the northwest of Seoul.
In winter a cold wind blows in from the northwest.
The small lake is in the northwest of the park.
If you walk ten minutes to the northwest, you will find it.
Dark clouds are rushing in quickly from the northwest.
The compass needle is pointing to the northwest.

explain: 한국의 겨울 찬 바람은 북서쪽에서 오는 일이 많아서 날씨 이야기에 자주 나와요. 'ㄱ' 받침 뒤라서 '서'가 [써]로 세게 소리 나고, [북써쪽]이라고 읽어요. 바람 이름은 '북서풍'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Cold winter winds in Korea often come from the northwest, so this word shows up in weather talk. After the final 'ㄱ' the 'ㅅ' of '서' is tensed, so it is read [buk-sseo-jjok]. The wind itself is called '북서풍'.

examples.en: Gangwon Province is to the northeast when seen from Seoul.
If you go northeast, you will reach the sea.
Last night the typhoon slowly passed toward the northeast.

examples.ko: 우리 집 북동쪽에 큰 시장이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a big market northeast of our house.
The morning sun comes in through the northeast window.

examples.ko: 지도에서 북동쪽 끝까지 기차로 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can go to the far northeast of the map by train.

explain: 같은 방향을 '동북쪽'이라고도 해요. '동북아시아'처럼 이름이 굳은 말에서는 '동북'을 써요. [북똥쪽]으로 소리 나는 것도 외워 두세요.
explain_en: The same direction can also be '동북쪽'. Set names like '동북아시아' (Northeast Asia) use '동북'. Also remember it is pronounced [buk-ttong-jjok].

examples.en: My father goes to the golf course every Sunday.
The golf course in our town is in the mountains.
The scenery at this golf course is really nice.
It takes an hour by car to get to the golf course.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 회사 사람들과 골프장을 예약했어요.
examples.en: I booked the golf course with my coworkers for this weekend.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 골프장이 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the golf course closed.

explain: 골프는 '치다'와 함께 써서 '골프를 치다'라고 해요. 골프장에서 한 바퀴 도는 것을 '라운딩'이라고도 하고, 골프장 이름 뒤에는 'CC'를 자주 붙여요. '골프 치러 가다'처럼 목적을 말할 때는 '골프장' 없이도 돼요.
explain_en: Golf pairs with '치다' (hit), so you say '골프를 치다'. Playing a round at the course is also called '라운딩', and course names often end in 'CC'. For purpose you can say '골프 치러 가다' (go to play golf) without mentioning the course.

examples.en: The name is written on the front of the card.
The coin my friend tossed came up heads.
Please write your answers only on the front of the test paper.

examples.ko: 책 앞면에 예쁜 그림이 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: A pretty picture is drawn on the front of the book.
Please write the address on the front of the envelope.

examples.ko: 옷 앞면에 작은 단추가 세 개 달려 있어요.
examples.en: The front of the shirt has three small buttons.

explain: 발음은 [암면]이에요. '앞'의 받침이 [ㅂ]으로 바뀌고 'ㅁ' 앞에서 다시 [ㅁ]이 돼요. 방향은 '앞쪽', 평평한 물건의 한 면은 '앞면'이라고 해요. '뒷면'과 짝으로 외우세요.
explain_en: It is pronounced [am-myeon]: the final 'ㅍ' of '앞' becomes [ㅂ], then turns into [ㅁ] before 'ㅁ'. Direction is '앞쪽' (front direction), while one side of a flat object is '앞면'. Learn it as a pair with '뒷면'.

examples.en: Every night I hear music from the next room.

examples.ko: 제 친구가 기숙사에서 제 옆방에 살아요.
examples.en: My friend lives in the room next to mine in the dormitory.

examples.ko: 호텔 옆방에 저희 부모님이 묵고 계세요.
examples.en: My parents are staying in the room next to mine at the hotel.
I moved the luggage to the next room to clean.

examples.ko: 옆방에 사는 친구가 가끔 라면을 빌려 가요.
examples.en: The friend who lives next door sometimes borrows ramyeon from me.
The door to the next room was open, so I peeked in.

explain: 건물이 다르면 '옆집', 같은 건물 안의 방이면 '옆방'이라고 해요. 기숙사, 고시원, 호텔에서 소리 이야기를 할 때 특히 자주 써요. 발음은 [엽빵]이에요.
explain_en: A different building next door is '옆집', while a room in the same building is 'yeopbang'. It comes up a lot in talk about noise in dorms, small rented rooms and hotels. It is pronounced [yeop-ppang].

examples.en: If you take the local bus, it is five minutes to the subway station.
The local bus in our neighborhood has a cheap fare.
I go to work by local bus every morning.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 마을버스가 오지 않아서 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: The local bus did not come on a rainy day, so I walked.
There is a local bus stop in front of my house.
I got off the local bus and transferred to the subway.

explain: 큰길을 오가는 '시내버스'보다 작고, 동네와 지하철역을 이어 줘요. 서울에서는 지하철이나 다른 버스와 환승이 되는 경우가 많아요. '타다', '내리다', '갈아타다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is smaller than a main-road city bus ('시내버스') and links neighborhoods with subway stations. In Seoul you can often transfer to the subway or other buses with it. It goes with '타다' (ride), '내리다' (get off) and '갈아타다' (transfer).

examples.en: I planned the travel route in advance.

examples.ko: 이 루트로 가면 시간이 덜 걸려요.
examples.en: If you take this route, it takes less time.

examples.ko: 처음 가 본 등산 루트가 너무 어려웠어요.
examples.en: The hiking route I tried for the first time was too difficult.
The road is jammed, so let's look for another route.
Please tell me the fastest route.

examples.ko: 배송 루트가 복잡해서 하루 더 걸려요.
examples.en: The delivery route is complicated, so it takes one more day.

explain: '길'이나 '경로'보다 여행, 등산, 배송처럼 거쳐 갈 곳을 정해 둔 코스에 가까워요. '루트를 짜다', '루트를 정하다'처럼 같이 써요. 수학에서 √ 기호도 '루트'라고 읽어서 헷갈릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '길' (road) or '경로' (path), 'ruteu' is closer to a planned course for travel, hiking or delivery. It pairs with '루트를 짜다' and '루트를 정하다' (plan/decide a route). In math the √ sign is also read 'ruteu', so watch the context.

examples.ko: 앱 화면 상단에 검색 메뉴가 있어요.
examples.en: The search menu is at the top of the app screen.

examples.ko: 페이지 상단을 한 번 눌러 보세요.
examples.en: Try pressing the top of the page once.
A sign hangs at the top of the building.
Write the title first at the top of the table.
Usually the top of a map points north.

examples.ko: 포스터 상단 오른쪽에 행사 날짜가 있어요.
examples.en: The event date is at the top right of the poster.

explain: '위쪽'보다 딱딱한 말이라 화면, 표, 건물, 안내문 설명에서 자주 써요. 반대말은 '하단'이에요. '화면 상단', '상단 메뉴'처럼 같이 나오는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than plain '위쪽' (upper side) and is common when describing screens, tables, buildings and notices. The opposite is '하단' (bottom part). It tends to appear in fixed combinations like '화면 상단' (top of the screen) and '상단 메뉴' (top menu).

examples.en: Incheon International Airport is really big and clean.
It takes an hour by bus to get to the international airport.
My hometown Busan also has an international airport.

examples.ko: 저는 김포 국제공항에서 친구를 두 시간 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited two hours for my friend at Gimpo International Airport.

examples.ko: 새 국제공항이 내년 봄에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: A new international airport opens next spring.
There are many hotels near the international airport.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '공항'이라고만 해도 충분해요. '국제공항'은 공항 이름이나 뉴스, 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 해외로 가는 비행기는 '국제선', 나라 안에서 타는 비행기는 '국내선'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In everyday talk just '공항' (airport) is enough. 'Gukje gonghang' shows up in airport names, news and signs. Flights abroad are '국제선' (international) and domestic ones are '국내선'.

examples.en: The motor of this fan is broken.
At night the motor sound is too loud.
We attached a small motor to the boat.
The repairman replaced the motor with a new one.
There is a motor inside a washing machine.
Electric cars run on a motor instead of an engine.

explain: 전기로 돌아가는 장치는 '모터', 기름을 태워 움직이는 장치는 '엔진'이에요. 전동 킥보드와 전기 자전거는 모터, 오토바이는 엔진이에요. '전동기'라는 한자어도 있지만 일상에서는 '모터'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '모터가 돌다', '모터가 고장 나다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A device spun by electricity is a 'motor', while one that burns fuel is an 'engine' (엔진). Electric scooters and e-bikes have motors, while motorcycles have engines. There is also the Sino-Korean word '전동기', but in daily life '모터' is used far more. It pairs with '모터가 돌다' (the motor spins) and '모터가 고장 나다' (the motor breaks).

examples.ko: 길 반대편에 작은 약국이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small pharmacy on the opposite side of the street.
To take the subway, please go to the opposite platform.
I sat on the chair opposite the window.
You have to take the bus from the other side.
Yesterday I walked all the way to the other side of the lake.
In the debate, my friend and I took opposite sides.

explain: '건너편'은 길이나 강처럼 건너야 하는 곳의 맞은쪽이고, 반대편은 건너지 않아도 '이쪽이 아닌 쪽'이면 써요. 지하철 승강장은 '반대편 승강장'이라고 해요. 장소뿐 아니라 팀이나 의견처럼 서로 맞서는 쪽에도 써요.
explain_en: '건너편' is the far side of something you cross, like a road or river, while 반대편 is simply 'the side that is not this one', with no crossing needed. A subway platform is called '반대편 승강장'. It also works for opposing teams or opinions, not only places.

examples.ko: 여행 중에 유명한 스타디움 투어를 했어요.
examples.en: On my trip I took a tour of a famous stadium.

examples.ko: 경기 시작 전에 스타디움 앞에서 만나요.
examples.en: Let's meet in front of the stadium before the match starts.

examples.ko: 경기 날에는 스타디움이 사람들로 가득 찼어요.
examples.en: On match day the stadium was full of people.
This stadium holds fifty thousand people.
There are many good restaurants near the stadium.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 큰 스타디움에서 콘서트를 열었어요.
examples.en: That singer held a concert at a big stadium.

explain: 일상에서는 '경기장'이 더 흔하고, 스타디움은 이름에 붙이거나 크고 멋진 경기장을 말할 때 자주 써요. '운동장'은 학교나 동네의 넓은 땅이라 느낌이 달라요. 종목을 붙여 '야구장', '축구장'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: In daily talk '경기장' is the more common word; 스타디움 shows up in names and for big, impressive venues. '운동장' is a school or neighborhood field, so it feels different. You can also add the sport: '야구장' (baseball field), '축구장' (soccer field).

examples.en: A river flows along the border between the two countries.
We put up a fence on the boundary line of the land with our neighbor.
For safety, please do not cross the boundary line.
The ball went outside the boundary line.
The boundary line is drawn in red on the map.

examples.ko: 도시와 시골의 경계선이 점점 흐려지고 있어요.
examples.en: The line between city and countryside is getting blurrier.

explain: '국경'은 나라와 나라 사이에만 쓰지만, 경계선은 땅·운동장·도시처럼 어디에나 쓸 수 있어요. 눈에 보이는 선이 없어도 '선을 넘다'라고 하면 예의나 규칙을 어긴다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: '국경' (national border) is only for countries, while 경계선 fits land, sports fields, cities, anything. Even when no line is visible, '선을 넘다' (cross the line) can mean breaking manners or rules.

examples.ko: 장 본 짐을 차 트렁크에 넣어요.
examples.en: I put the groceries I bought in the car trunk.
The trunk is small, so the bag does not fit.

examples.ko: 짐을 실어야 하니까 트렁크를 열어 주세요.
examples.en: I need to load the luggage, so please open the trunk.

examples.ko: 비가 오는데 우산을 트렁크에 두고 왔어요.
examples.en: It is raining, but I left my umbrella in the trunk.
This car has a spacious trunk.
Dad took the camping chairs out of the trunk.

explain: 한국어에서 트렁크는 보통 승용차 뒤쪽 짐 넣는 곳을 말해요. 여행 가방은 '캐리어'라고 하고, 트럭 뒤쪽은 '짐칸'이라고 해요. 영어의 trunk처럼 코끼리 코나 나무줄기로는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: In Korean 트렁크 usually means the storage space at the back of a car. A suitcase is a '캐리어', and the back of a truck is a '짐칸'. It is not used for an elephant's trunk or a tree trunk like in English.

examples.ko: 서울에서 부산으로 가는 다음 항공편은 몇 시예요?
examples.en: What time is the next flight from Seoul to Busan?
The flight was canceled, so I stayed one more day.
There are many flights to Jeju Island.
This flight I booked is a direct flight.
In the vacation season, please book your flight in advance.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 항공편이 두 시간 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the flight was delayed by two hours.

explain: '비행기'는 타는 물건 자체이고, 항공편은 정해진 시간표의 한 편을 말해요. '항공편이 취소됐어요', '항공편을 예약했어요'처럼 쓰고, 표 자체는 '항공권'이라고 해요. 소포를 '항공편으로 보내다'처럼 비행기로 보낸다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: '비행기' is the plane itself, while 항공편 is one scheduled flight on a timetable. You say '항공편이 취소됐어요' (the flight was canceled) or '항공편을 예약했어요' (I booked a flight), and the ticket itself is '항공권'. It can also mean 'by air', as in a parcel sent '항공편으로'.

examples.ko: 끝없는 들판 너머로 지평선이 펼쳐져 있어요.
examples.en: The horizon stretches out beyond the endless fields.

examples.ko: 저녁이 되자 지평선 너머로 해가 졌어요.
examples.en: When evening came, the sun set beyond the horizon.

examples.ko: 산이 없는 넓은 평야에서는 지평선이 잘 보여요.
examples.en: On a wide plain without mountains you can see the horizon well.
The road continues far away to the horizon.

examples.ko: 하늘 아래 지평선에 붉은 노을이 번졌어요.
examples.en: Red sunset glow spread across the horizon under the sky.

examples.ko: 차를 타고 가도 지평선이 가까워지지 않아요.
examples.en: Even riding in a car, the horizon does not get any closer.

explain: 바다 끝에 보이는 선은 '수평선', 땅 끝에 보이는 선은 지평선이라고 구분해요. 한국은 산이 많아서 지평선을 보기 어렵고, 김제 같은 넓은 평야에서 볼 수 있다고들 해요.
explain_en: The line at the end of the sea is '수평선', and the line at the end of land is 지평선. Korea has many mountains, so a horizon is hard to see; people say you can see it on wide plains like Gimje.

examples.en: Busan is at the southeastern end of Korea.

examples.ko: 우리 방은 남동쪽 창문으로 햇빛이 들어와요.
examples.en: In my room, sunlight comes in through the southeast window.
The news says a typhoon is coming up from the southeast.

examples.ko: 우리가 묵을 호텔은 역의 남동쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: The hotel where we will stay is southeast of the station.

examples.ko: 지도를 보면서 남동쪽 방향으로 쭉 가세요.
examples.en: Looking at the map, go straight toward the southeast.

examples.ko: 집이 남동쪽을 향해 있어서 아침이 밝아요.
examples.en: The house faces southeast, so the mornings are bright.

explain: '남동쪽'과 '동남쪽'을 둘 다 써요. 일기예보·지도에서는 '남동풍'처럼 '남동'을 쓰고, '동남아시아'처럼 굳은 이름에는 '동남'이 들어가요. 영어 southeast와 같은 순서가 '남동', 반대 순서가 '동남'이에요. 길을 설명할 때는 '남동쪽 방향'처럼 방향을 붙이기도 해요.
explain_en: Both '남동쪽' and '동남쪽' are used. Forecasts and maps use '남동' (as in '남동풍', southeast wind), while set names like '동남아시아' (Southeast Asia) contain '동남'. '남동' has the same order as English 'southeast' (south first); '동남' is the reverse. When giving directions you can add 방향: '남동쪽 방향'.

examples.en: There are empty seats at the back of the bus.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 뒷부분이 앞부분보다 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: In this movie, the last part is more fun than the first part.
I have not read the last part of the book yet.

examples.ko: 저 건물 뒷부분에 작은 주차장이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small parking lot at the back of that building.
I fell yesterday, so the back of my head hurts.
I forgot the end of the story, so I looked it up again.

explain: 반대말은 '앞부분'이에요. 공간만 말할 때는 '뒤쪽'도 자주 써요. 뒷부분은 [뒤뿌분]으로 읽고, '뒤'와 '부분' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가요.
explain_en: The opposite is '앞부분' (front part). For plain space, '뒤쪽' (the back side) is also common. 뒷부분 is read [뒤뿌분], with a 사이시옷 (ㅅ) between '뒤' and '부분'.

examples.en: Snow has piled up on the upper part of the mountain.
I dropped it on the floor, so the top of the cup broke.
I attached a name tag to the upper part of the door.
Please fold the top of the paper in half.
There is a bird's nest at the top of the tree.
I drew a blue sky in the upper part of the picture.

explain: '위부분'이 아니라 '윗부분'이라고 써요. '윗'은 '아랫'과 짝이고, '윗사람'·'윗옷'·'윗입술'에도 같은 모양이 나와요. 윗부분은 [위뿌분]으로 읽고, 반대말은 '아랫부분'이에요.
explain_en: It is written '윗부분', not '위부분'. '윗' pairs with '아랫', and the same form appears in '윗사람' (superior), '윗옷' (top clothes), and '윗입술' (upper lip). 윗부분 is read [위뿌분], and the opposite is '아랫부분'.

examples.en: A police car is parked in front of my house.
A police car just passed with its siren on.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에 경찰차가 두 대 왔어요.
examples.en: Two police cars came to the scene of the accident.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 경찰차를 보면 아주 좋아해요.
examples.en: My child loves it when they see a police car.
I drove slowly behind the police car.

examples.ko: 경찰차 소리가 들리면 차들이 길을 비켜 줘요.
examples.en: When cars hear a police car, they make way.

explain: 거리를 돌며 순찰하는 차는 뉴스에서 '순찰차'라고도 자주 불러요. 일상에서는 '경찰차'가 가장 흔해요. '소방차', '구급차'처럼 '차'를 붙여 만든 말이 많아요.
explain_en: A car that patrols the streets is also often called '순찰차' (patrol car) in the news. In daily life '경찰차' is the most common word. Many similar words add '차', like '소방차' (fire truck) and '구급차' (ambulance).

examples.en: For safety, hold the steering wheel with both hands.

examples.ko: 이 차는 운전대가 너무 무거워서 힘들어요.
examples.en: The steering wheel of this car is too heavy, so it is hard.
On cold winter mornings the steering wheel is cold.
My father is holding the steering wheel right now.

examples.ko: 주차할 때는 운전대를 천천히 돌려 보세요.
examples.en: When you park, try turning the steering wheel slowly.
Do not take the wheel when you are sleepy.

explain: 일상에서는 '핸들'이라고 더 자주 말해요. 영어 handle에서 온 말인데, 영어의 handle은 손잡이라서 자동차 운전대는 steering wheel이라고 해요. 그래서 영어를 쓰는 사람에게 '핸들'이라고 하면 못 알아들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: In daily speech Koreans say '핸들' more often. It comes from the English word handle, but in English a handle is a grip, and the car part is called a steering wheel. So an English speaker may not understand Korean '핸들'.

examples.ko: 길을 아니까 오늘은 제가 운전석에 앉을게요.
examples.en: I know the way, so I will sit in the driver's seat today.

examples.ko: 차 운전석 문이 갑자기 안 열려요.
examples.en: The driver's door of the car suddenly will not open.

examples.ko: 키가 작아서 운전석 의자를 앞으로 당겼어요.
examples.en: I am short, so I moved the driver's seat forward.

examples.ko: 높은 차는 운전석에 앉으면 시야가 넓어요.
examples.en: In a tall car, you get a wide view when you sit in the driver's seat.
There is a map on the seat next to the driver.

examples.ko: 택시 기사님이 운전석에서 내려서 문을 열어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The taxi driver got out of the driver's seat and opened the door for me.

explain: 운전석 옆자리는 '조수석'이라고 해요. '조수'는 돕는 사람이라는 뜻인데, 지금은 운전을 돕지 않아도 그대로 써요. 한국은 차가 길 오른쪽으로 달려서 운전석이 왼쪽에 있어요.
explain_en: The seat next to the driver is called '조수석'. '조수' means 'assistant', but the word stays even when the person is not helping to drive. Korea drives on the right side of the road, so the driver's seat is on the left.

examples.en: The baby is sleeping soundly in the stroller.
In the evening I walked in the park pushing the stroller.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터가 없어서 유모차를 들고 계단을 올랐어요.
examples.en: There was no elevator, so I carried the stroller up the stairs.

examples.ko: 유모차가 지나갈 수 있게 비켜 주세요.
examples.en: Please move aside so the stroller can pass.
I bought a stroller my friend used for cheap.
This stroller gets very small when you fold it.

explain: 한국에서는 가볍게 접히는 것을 '휴대용 유모차', 튼튼하고 큰 것을 '디럭스 유모차'라고 구분해서 불러요. 동사는 '유모차를 밀다', '유모차를 끌다'처럼 밀다·끌다를 써요.
explain_en: In Korea a light, foldable one is called a '휴대용 유모차' (portable stroller) and a sturdy, big one a '디럭스 유모차' (deluxe stroller). The verbs are 밀다 (push) and 끌다 (pull): '유모차를 밀다'.

examples.en: At low tide I picked up shells at the beachside.

examples.ko: 저녁 바람을 맞으며 해변가를 따라 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly along the beachside in the evening breeze.

examples.ko: 이 동네 해변가에 예쁜 카페가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many pretty cafés along the beach in this town.
In summer the children play happily at the beachside.
For this vacation I booked a place to stay by the beach.
I watched the sun rise at the beachside.

explain: '해변'만 써도 같은 곳을 말해요. '해변'에 '가'가 또 붙어 뜻이 겹치지만 말할 때는 자주 써요. 바닷가는 '바닷가에서 살다'처럼 사는 곳에도 쓰고, 해변은 놀러 가는 모래사장 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Just '해변' can refer to the same place. 해변가 adds '가' (edge) to 해변, so the meaning overlaps, but people say it a lot in speech. '바닷가' also works for where people live ('바닷가에서 살다'), while 해변 feels more like a sandy beach for leisure.

examples.en: There are many old books and toys in the attic room.
Our attic room is narrow but very cozy.
My grandmother's house in the countryside has an attic room.
The stairs going up to the attic room are very steep.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 아이들이 다락방에서 숨바꼭질을 해요.
examples.en: On rainy days the kids play hide-and-seek in the attic room.

examples.ko: 저는 다락방에 누워서 만화책을 읽는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: I like lying in the attic room and reading comic books.

explain: '다락'은 지붕 아래 짐을 두는 공간이고, 그곳에 이불이나 책상을 두고 방처럼 쓰면 다락방이라고 해요. 요즘 아파트에는 거의 없어서 옛날 집이나 동화·드라마에서 자주 만나요. [다락빵]으로 읽어요.
explain_en: '다락' is the storage space under the roof; when people put bedding or a desk there and use it like a room, it becomes a 다락방. Modern apartments rarely have one, so you meet it in old houses, fairy tales, and dramas. It is read [다락빵].

examples.ko: 차를 탈 때는 뒷좌석에도 안전벨트를 매세요.
examples.en: When you ride in a car, wear a seat belt in the back seat too.
A young child is safer sitting in the back seat.
I put the heavy bag on the back seat first.

examples.ko: 이 차는 뒷좌석이 넓어서 오래 타도 편해요.
examples.en: This car has a spacious back seat, so it is comfortable even for long rides.
I left my umbrella in the back seat of the taxi.
My friends are singing happily in the back seat.

explain: 택시에서는 보통 뒷좌석에 앉고, 친한 사람이 운전하는 차에서는 앞의 '조수석'에 앉기도 해요. 뒷좌석도 안전벨트를 매라는 안내가 자주 나와요. 교실이나 버스의 뒤쪽 자리는 '뒷자리'를 써요.
explain_en: In a taxi people usually sit in the back seat, while in a friend's car you may sit up front in the '조수석' (passenger seat). Announcements often remind you to buckle up in the back seat too. For the back seats in a classroom or on a bus, use '뒷자리'.

examples.en: The marathon starting point is in front of City Hall.
The starting point of this trip is Seoul Station.

examples.ko: 우리 모두 출발점에서 열 시에 만나요.
examples.en: Let's all meet at the starting point at ten.

examples.ko: 한 바퀴를 걷고 출발점으로 다시 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I walked one lap and came back to the starting point.

examples.ko: 등산 출발점까지 버스로 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes thirty minutes by bus to the hiking starting point.

examples.ko: 이 길은 올레길 일 코스의 출발점이에요.
examples.en: This path is the starting point of Olle Trail Course 1.

explain: 같은 자리를 '시작점'이라고도 하지만 길이나 경기 이야기에서는 출발점이 더 자연스러워요. 달리기처럼 땅에 그은 선은 '출발선'이라고 해서 더 구체적이에요. 반대말은 '도착점'이에요.
explain_en: The same spot can be called '시작점' too, but for roads and races 출발점 sounds more natural. The line drawn on the ground for a race is '출발선', which is more specific. The opposite is '도착점' (finish point).

examples.en: At night the building's entrance door is locked.
This building's entrance door is over there.
Please do not leave luggage in front of the entrance door.

examples.ko: 출입문 옆에 우산을 넣는 통이 있어요.
examples.en: Next to the entrance door there is a bin for umbrellas.
A notice about the day off is posted on the entrance door.

examples.ko: 이 가게 출입문은 자동으로 열리고 닫혀요.
examples.en: This shop's entrance door opens and closes automatically.

explain: 내 집 문은 '현관문', 건물·가게·학교처럼 사람이 많이 드나드는 문은 출입문이라고 구분해요. '출입'은 '나가고 들어오는 것'이라 [추림문]으로 이어서 읽어요.
explain_en: Your own home's door is a '현관문', while the door of a building, shop, or school that many people pass through is a 출입문. It is read connected as [추림문].

examples.en: I went up the mountain by cable car.
The view looking down from the cable car is really wonderful.
I bought two cable car tickets.
When the wind is strong, the cable car stops.
Excuse me, where is the cable car boarding area?
The line waiting for the cable car was very long.

explain: 한국 관광지에서 자주 만나요. 남산·설악산 케이블카나 여수 바다 위 케이블카처럼 앞에 장소를 붙여 말해요. 표를 살 때는 올라갔다 내려오는 '왕복'과 한 방향만 가는 '편도'를 골라요.
explain_en: You meet it often at Korean tourist spots. People put the place name first: Namsan or Seoraksan cable car, or the cable car over the sea in Yeosu. When buying a ticket you pick '왕복' (round trip) or '편도' (one way).

examples.en: I arrived home, opened the front door, and went in.

examples.ko: 현관문 앞에 택배 상자가 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A delivery box is sitting in front of the front door.
I always lock the front door when I go out.
The front door slammed shut in the wind.
For security, I changed the front door password.
I hear someone knocking on the front door.

explain: 한국 집은 현관에서 신발을 벗고 들어가요. 그래서 문 안쪽의 신발 벗는 공간을 '현관'이라고 따로 불러요. 요즘은 열쇠 대신 '도어락' 번호로 여는 집이 많아요.
explain_en: In a Korean home you take off your shoes at the entrance. That is why the shoe-removing space just inside the door has its own name, '현관'. These days many homes open with a '도어락' (digital door lock) code instead of a key.

examples.en: If you sit in the front seat, you can see the board well.
Adults sit in the front seat of the car.
If you sit in the front seats at the cinema, your neck hurts.
The friend in the front seat waved.
The front seat on that bus is empty.

examples.ko: 콘서트는 앞자리 표가 제일 먼저 팔려요.
examples.en: For concerts, the front-seat tickets sell first.

explain: 교실·극장·버스처럼 자리가 줄지어 있는 곳에서는 '앞자리'가 자연스러워요. 차 안에서는 '앞좌석'이나 '조수석'도 써요. 반대말은 '뒷자리'예요.
explain_en: In places where seats are lined up, like classrooms, theaters, and buses, 앞자리 sounds natural. Inside a car, '앞좌석' (front seat) or '조수석' (passenger seat) is also used. The opposite is '뒷자리'.

examples.en: It is dangerous to cross the center line when you drive.
A center line is painted in the middle of the road.
The car moved close to the center line.
The center line on Korean roads is usually yellow.
They repainted the center line because of the construction.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 중앙선이 잘 안 보여서 무서워요.
examples.en: When it rains the center line is hard to see, so it is scary.

explain: 중앙선은 노란색이고, 같은 방향으로 가는 차선은 흰색이에요. 중앙선을 넘는 위반은 '중앙선 침범'이라고 부르고, 사고 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The center line is yellow, and lines between lanes going the same direction are white. Breaking the rule by crossing it is called '중앙선 침범' (center line violation), which often appears in accident news.

en: back seat (in a bus or classroom)

examples.ko: 뒷자리에 앉은 사람이 큰 소리로 말해요.
examples.en: The person in the back seat talks loudly.
It is hard to see from the back seat in the classroom.
I sat alone in the back seat of the bus.
The back seat was empty, so I moved over there.
Mom put the child in the back seat of the car.
The class was boring, so I talked with the friend in the back seat.

explain: '뒷좌석'은 주로 차 안에서 쓰고, 뒷자리는 교실·버스·극장까지 널리 써요. 반대말은 '앞자리'예요. 학교 이야기에서는 뒷자리가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '뒷좌석' is mostly used inside a car, while 뒷자리 is used widely for classrooms, buses, and theaters too. The opposite is '앞자리'. In stories about school, 뒷자리 sounds more natural.

examples.en: There are many strange fish in the deep sea.
I learned to dive to see under the sea in person.

examples.ko: 바닷속은 소리가 거의 안 들려서 아주 조용해요.
examples.en: There is almost no sound under the sea, so it is very quiet.

examples.ko: 친구가 찍어 준 바닷속 사진이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The underwater photos my friend took are really pretty.
I saw a huge turtle under the sea off Jeju Island.
The deeper you go, the darker it gets under the sea.

explain: '바다 속'처럼 띄지 않고 '바닷속'으로 붙여 써요. 비슷한 '물속'은 수영장이나 강에도 쓰지만 바닷속은 바다에만 써요. '땅속', '산속'도 같은 방식으로 만든 말이에요.
explain_en: It is written as one word, '바닷속', not '바다 속'. The similar '물속' (in the water) also works for pools and rivers, but 바닷속 is only for the sea. '땅속' (underground) and '산속' (deep in the mountains) are made the same way.

examples.en: Lots of cargo trucks run on the highway.

examples.ko: 화물차 한 대가 짐을 싣고 있어요.
examples.en: A cargo truck is loading goods.

examples.ko: 화물차는 이 길로 다니면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Cargo trucks must not use this road.
The cargo truck driver unloaded the goods for us.
On moving day I rented a small cargo truck.

examples.ko: 새벽에는 화물차 소리 때문에 잠을 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up at dawn because of the sound of cargo trucks.

explain: '트럭'이라고도 많이 불러요. 법이나 뉴스에서는 '화물차', 일상에서는 '트럭'이 더 흔해요. 아주 작은 것은 '소형 트럭'이나 '1톤 트럭'이라고 해요.
explain_en: People often say '트럭' (truck) too. Laws and the news use 화물차, while daily conversation uses 트럭 more. A very small one is called a '소형 트럭' (small truck) or a '1톤 트럭' (1-ton truck).

examples.ko: 주말에 가족과 과천에 있는 대공원에 갔어요.
examples.en: On the weekend I went to the large park in Gwacheon with my family.

examples.ko: 대공원은 걸어서 한 바퀴 도는 데 두 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes two hours to walk around the large park.

examples.ko: 이 대공원 안에 큰 동물원이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a big zoo inside this large park.

examples.ko: 대공원 입구에서 자전거를 한 시간 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I rented a bicycle for an hour at the entrance of the large park.
In spring, many flowers bloom in the large park.
You can get to the large park by subway.

explain: 대공원은 보통 이름에 붙어요. '서울대공원'처럼 공원 이름으로 쓰기도 하고, 일반 공원보다 훨씬 넓은 공원을 가리키기도 해요. 작은 동네 공원은 그냥 '공원'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 대공원 usually appears as part of a name. It can be a proper name like '서울대공원' (Seoul Grand Park), or it can point to a park much bigger than an ordinary one. A small neighborhood park is just '공원'.

examples.en: The road continues in a straight line.
I drew a straight line in my notebook with a ruler.
The children are standing in a straight line on the playground.
I laid the pencils in a straight line on the desk.
Try connecting the two points with a straight line.

examples.ko: 집에서 학교까지 일직선이라서 길을 잃을 일이 없어요.
examples.en: It is a straight line from home to school, so you cannot get lost.

explain: '직선'과 거의 같지만, 일직선은 '한 줄로 쭉 곧게'라는 느낌이 강해요. 그래서 줄을 서거나 길이 곧게 이어질 때 '일직선으로'를 많이 써요. [일찍썬]으로 읽어요.
explain_en: It is close to '직선' (straight line), but 일직선 stresses 'one line, perfectly straight'. That is why '일직선으로' is common for lining up or for a road running straight. It is read [일찍썬].

examples.en: If you sit in the front row, you can see the stage well.
Shorter students stand in the front row.
I bought a front row ticket for the show at a high price.
The person in the front row raised their hand.
The front row is already full.
I could not hear from the back row, so I moved to the front row.

explain: 앞줄은 맨 앞의 줄을 말하고, '앞자리'는 앞쪽 자리들을 두루 말하는 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '뒷줄'이에요. 극장·교실·콘서트에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: 앞줄 means the very first row, while '앞자리' loosely refers to the seats toward the front. The opposite is '뒷줄' (back row). It is common for theaters, classrooms, and concerts.

examples.en: Every evening I took a light walk along the lakeside.

examples.ko: 호숫가에 분위기 좋은 작은 카페가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small café with a nice mood at the lakeside.
In the morning I saw a family of ducks at the lakeside.
I rested sitting on a bench at the lakeside.
On the weekend we pitched a tent at the lakeside and camped.
The lakeside breeze was cool, so I felt better.

explain: 받침이 없는 말 뒤에는 사이시옷이 들어가 '호숫가', '바닷가'가 되고, 받침이 있는 '강' 뒤에서는 '강가'로 그대로 써요. 물 가까운 곳은 이렇게 '물 이름 + 가'로 만들어요. [호수까]로 읽어요.
explain_en: After a word with no final consonant, a 사이시옷 (ㅅ) is added, giving '호숫가' and '바닷가'; after '강', which has a final consonant, it stays '강가'. Places near water are made this way: water name + 가. It is read [호수까].
